question: How does a SIM swap or SIM cloning fraud work?
retrieved (file p.page): Beavare.pdf p.12 | Beavare.pdf p.11 | Beavare.pdf p.12 | RBI (FAQ1) Direction.pdf p.1 | Management of Assets-Liabilities.pdf p.32
bot_answer: A SIM swap or SIM cloning fraud involves fraudsters gaining access to a customer's Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) card or obtaining a duplicate SIM card (including electronic-SIM) for the registered mobile number connected to the customer's bank account [1]. They then use the One-Time Password (OTP) received on the duplicate SIM to carry out unauthorized transactions [1]. Fraudsters often collect personal or identity details by posing as telephone/mobile network staff and offering fake benefits such as free SIM upgrades from 3G to 4G [1].
expected_answer: Fraudsters gain access to the customer's SIM card or obtain a duplicate SIM (including e-SIM) for the mobile number registered with the bank account, and use it to receive OTPs and make unauthorised transactions.
